key_insight: The paper turns Fourier-spectrum analysis of parameterized quantum circuits into a concrete gate-placement rule for making a desired Fourier coefficient reachable.
engineering_relevance: It gives quantum hardware and QNN designers a practical way to place local rotations and entanglers, based on the interaction graph, to improve expressivity for target tasks.
method: Use the adjoint action of the encoding generator to decompose operator space into frequency-indexed invariant planes.
Express each Fourier coefficient as bilinear projections of the effective state and observable onto the corresponding planes.
Derive a placement rule for Pauli readouts with commuting two-qubit entanglers that identifies where rotations and entangling layers should be placed.
evidence_signal: The proposed design was validated with a placement ablation and downstream experiments on PDEBench regression and physics-informed Maxwell field modeling, with robustness tests under moderate simulated gate noise and damping.
watch_item: The rule is derived for a single encoding layer and specific Pauli/commuting-entangler settings, so broader circuits or hardware-native gate sets may need re-derivation.
paper_title: Fourier-Geometric Circuit Design for Gate and Entanglement Placement in Quantum Neural Networks
